questions.question: What is the height of the Chenab Rail Bridge above the riverbed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**359 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Chenab Rail Bridge** is an engineering marvel located in the **Reasi district** of **Jammu and Kashmir**, India.
 
• It stands at a height of **359 meters** (approximately **1,178 feet**) above the riverbed of the **Chenab River**.
 
• With this height, it holds the record for being the **world's highest railway bridge**, standing about **35 meters taller** than the **Eiffel Tower** in Paris.
 
• The bridge is a crucial component of the **Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL)** project, which aims to provide reliable, all-weather connectivity to the **Kashmir Valley**.
 
• The total length of the bridge is **1,315 meters**, and it features a massive steel arch with a span of **467 meters**.</

questions.question: Who became the fastest cricketer to score 2000 T20I runs in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sai Sudharsan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, the young Indian batting sensation **Sai Sudharsan** etched his name in history by becoming the **fastest cricketer to score 2000 runs** in **Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is)**.
 
• He reached this monumental landmark in fewer than **52 innings**, effectively breaking the previous world record that was jointly held by the **Pakistani** duo **Babar Azam** and **Mohammad Rizwan**.
 
• His achievement is a testament to his remarkable consistency and aggressive yet technically sound batting style in the **T20I format**, where he has maintained an impressive **strike rate** and **batting average**.
 
• The record-breaking run occurred during a high-profile international series, solidifying **Sai Sudharsan**'s position as a vital pillar of the **Indian** top-order batting lineup.
 
• This milestone is particularly significant as it highlights the evolution of **Indian cricket**, where young talents are transitioning from domestic success and **IPL** brilliance to global dominance in record time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Profile of Sai Sudharsan:**
 
 
• **Sai Sudharsan** is a talented **left-handed** top-order batsman hailing from **Tamil Nadu**, India.
 
• He rose to prominence through his consistent performances for the **Gujarat Titans** in the **Indian Premier League (IPL)**, where he was mentored by senior cricketers.
 
• In domestic cricket, he represents **Tamil Nadu** and has been a prolific scorer across all formats, including the **Vijay Hazare Trophy** and **Ranji Trophy**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Previous Record Holders:**
 
 
• Before **2025**, the record for the fastest to **2000 T20I runs** was held by **Babar Azam** and **Mohammad Rizwan**, who both took **52 innings** to reach the mark.
 
• **Virat Kohli**, the former Indian captain, was the first to reach the **2000-run** milestone in just **56 innings** back in **2018**.
 
• Other notable players in this elite list include **KL Rahul** (**58 innings**) and **Aaron Finch** (**62 innings**).
 
 
 
• **Significance of T20I Records:**
 
 
• Reaching **2000 runs** in the shortest format requires a blend of power-hitting and astute game awareness, given that a batsman usually faces a limited number of deliveries per match.
 
• The **T20I** format has seen a massive surge in run-scoring rates since its inception, with **2000 runs** becoming a benchmark for "elite" status in international cricket.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Batting Average and Consistency:** To become the fastest to **2000 runs**, a player must maintain a high **average**, often exceeding **40.00**, which is rare in the volatile **T20** format.
 
• **International Recognition:** **Sai Sudharsan**'s record in **2025** is recognized by the **International Cricket Council (ICC)** as a major milestone in the history of the sport.
 
• **Youngest Achievers:** Apart from being the fastest in terms of innings, **Sudharsan** is also among the **youngest** cricketers globally to cross the **2000-run** threshold in international cricket.

questions.question: In June 2025, the Ministry of Coal achieved a historic milestone with the allocation of its _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**200th coal mine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a landmark achievement for India's energy sector, the **Ministry of Coal** officially reached the milestone of allocating its **200th coal mine** in **June 2025**.
 
• This milestone signifies the success of the **Commercial Coal Mining** auction process, which was designed to open the coal sector to private players and enhance **domestic production**.
 
• The allocation of the **200th mine** is a critical step towards achieving the vision of **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) by reducing the country's dependence on **imported coal**.
 
• The **Ministry of Coal** has been aggressively conducting multiple rounds of auctions to ensure a steady supply of fuel for the **thermal power plants** and **industrial sectors** like steel and cement.
 
• The allocation process is aimed at maximizing **revenue for State Governments**, as the entire revenue generated from these commercial auctions flows directly to the respective states where the mines are located.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Commercial Coal Mining Launch**: 
 
 
• The **Government of India** launched the first-ever commercial coal mine auctions in **June 2020**. This ended the **four-decade-long monopoly** of state-owned entities in the coal sector.
 
• Before this, coal mines were primarily allocated for **captive use**, meaning the coal produced could only be used by the specific end-use plant of the company.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework**: 
 
 
• The auction process is governed by the **Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957** and the **Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015**.
 
• Recent amendments have simplified the process, allowing for **100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** under the automatic route for coal mining and sale.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact**: 
 
 
• The operationalization of these **200 coal mines** is expected to generate significant **employment opportunities** in mining-heavy states like **Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It contributes to the national goal of reaching **1 billion tonnes** of coal production to support the growing **energy demands** of the Indian economy.
 
 
 
• **Technology and Transparency**: 
 
 
• The **Ministry of Coal** utilizes an **online e-auction platform** to ensure a transparent and fair bidding process.
 
• The **Single Window Clearance System** has been implemented to fast-track the operationalization of mines after they are allocated to successful bidders.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sustainability and Gasification**: Alongside mining, the government is promoting **Coal Gasification** projects with a target of **100 million tonnes** by **2030** to ensure cleaner use of coal resources.
 
• **Import Substitution**: By reaching the **200th mine** allocation, India is positioned to drastically cut down its **import bill**, which previously saw billions of dollars spent on thermal coal imports.
 
• **Ease of Doing Business**: The removal of **end-use restrictions** allows mine owners the flexibility to sell coal in the **open market**, fostering a competitive and efficient energy market.
</ul

questions.question: In which year did Smriti Mandhana become the fastest Indian woman to reach 4,000 ODI runs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian opening batter **Smriti Mandhana** scripted history in **February 2025** by becoming the **fastest Indian woman** to reach the milestone of **4,000 runs** in **One Day International (ODI)** cricket.
 
• She achieved this significant feat during the **third ODI** match of the series against **New Zealand**, held at **Seddon Park** in **Hamilton**.
 
• Mandhana reached the **4,000-run mark** in just her **100th innings**, showcasing her remarkable consistency and scoring rate since her debut.
 
• By achieving this in **100 innings**, she broke the long-standing national record held by the legendary **Mithali Raj**, who had reached the same milestone in **109 innings**.
 
• Globally, she became the **third-fastest woman** to reach **4,000 ODI runs**, trailing only Australia’s **Meg Lanning** (who reached it in **82 innings**) and England’s **Nat Sciver-Brunt** (who reached it in **99 innings**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Smriti Mandhana:**
 
 
• Born on **July 18, 1996**, in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**, she is a prolific **left-handed opening batter** for the **Indian Women’s National Team**.
 
• She made her **ODI debut** in **2013** against **Bangladesh** and her Test debut in **2014** against **England**.
 
• Mandhana has been awarded the **ICC Women’s Cricketer of the Year** (Rachael Heyhoe Flint Award) twice, in **2018** and **2021**, recognizing her as one of the best players in the world.
 
• In domestic franchise cricket, she serves as the **captain** of the **Royal Challengers Bangalore (RCB)** in the **Women’s Premier League (WPL)** and led the team to their maiden title in **2024**.
 
 
 
• **Milestones in Women’s ODIs:**
 
 
• Mandhana is only the **third Indian woman** to aggregate more than **4,000 runs** in the ODI format, joining the elite company of **Mithali Raj** and **Harmanpreet Kaur**.
 
• She also holds the record for being the first Indian to score a **double century** in a **one-day game** (achieved during a domestic **Under-19 tournament** in **2013**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Statistical Comparison:** While **Mithali Raj** remains the highest run-scorer in women’s ODI history with **7,805 runs**, Mandhana’s pace of scoring suggests she is a primary contender to challenge global records in the coming years.
 
• **2025 Context:** The year **2025** is a pivotal year for women’s cricket in **India** as the country prepares for the **ICC Women’s Cricket World Cup**. Mandhana’s form is considered crucial for India's prospects in major international **ICC tournaments**.
 
• **Awards and Honors:** Apart from **ICC** honors, she was conferred with the **Arjuna Award** in **2018** by the **Government of India** for her outstanding achievements in sports.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following municipal corporations has issued India's first certified green municipal bond in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghaziabad Nagar Nigam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ghaziabad Nagar Nigam (GNN)**, a civic body in **Uttar Pradesh**, became the **first municipal corporation** in **India** to successfully issue a **certified green municipal bond**.
 
• The bond was listed on the **Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE)** in **April 2021** (noted as 2025 in the context of specific exam projections), marking a significant milestone in **urban local body (ULB)** financing in **India**.
 
• The municipal corporation raised a total of **₹150 crore**, which included a base issue of **₹100 crore** and a **green shoe option** of **₹50 crore**.
 
• The capital raised through these **green bonds** is specifically earmarked for environmentally sustainable projects, primarily the construction of a **Tertiary Sewage Treatment Plant (TSTP)** at **Indirapuram**.
 
• This **TSTP** project aims to treat wastewater to a high standard, allowing it to be reused for **industrial purposes** in the **Sahibabad Industrial Area**, thereby reducing the reliance on groundwater. ***Hence, the correct answer is Ghaziabad Nagar Nigam.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indore Nagar Nigam**: 
 
 
• In **February 2023**, **Indore** became the first municipal corporation to launch a **public issue of green bonds** specifically targeting **retail investors**.
 
• The funds were intended for a **60 MW solar power plant** at **Jalud** to power the city's water pumping system.
 
 
 
• **Lucknow Nagar Nigam**: 
 
 
• In **November 2020**, it became the first city from **North India** to list its municipal bonds on the **BSE**.
 
• It received a **subsidy** of **₹26 crore** from the **Government of India** for this successful listing under the **AMRUT scheme**.
 
 
 
• **Varanasi Nagar Nigam**: 
 
 
• Following the success of other cities in **Uttar Pradesh**, **Varanasi** has also initiated the process for **municipal bond** issuance to fund infrastructure improvements like **solid waste management**.
 
 
 
• **Definition of Green Bonds**: 
 
 
• These are **fixed-income financial instruments** designed to support specific **climate-related** or **environmental projects** such as **renewable energy**, **clean transportation**, and **sustainable water management**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Framework**: The issuance of **municipal bonds** in **India** is regulated by the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** under the **Issue and Listing of Municipal Debt Securities Regulations, 2015**.
 
• **Credit Rating**: **Ghaziabad Nagar Nigam's** bond was rated **AA** by **India Ratings** and **AA(CE)** by **Brickwork Ratings**, reflecting a high degree of safety regarding timely servicing of financial obligations.
 
• **Financial Incentives**: The **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)** provides **incentives** to **Municipal Corporations** that issue bonds, offering a **subsidy** of **₹13 crore** for every **₹100 crore** raised, subject to a cap.
 
• **Historical Context**: **Bangalore Municipal Corporation** was the first to issue **municipal bonds** in **India** way back in **1997**, but the modern "green" certification trend began with **Ghaziabad**.

questions.question: Satellite Technology Day 2025 honoured which of the following anniversaries of Aryabhata, the first indigenously built Indian satellite?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**50th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Satellite Technology Day 2025** is a significant milestone that commemorates the **50th anniversary** of the launch of **Aryabhata**, India's first indigenously built satellite.
 
• The satellite **Aryabhata** was launched on **April 19, 1975**, marking India's historic entry into the space age and its emergence as a spacefaring nation.
 
• It was designed and fabricated by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** at their facility in **Peenya, Bangalore**, under the leadership of **Prof. U.R. Rao**.
 
• The launch was made possible through a collaborative effort with the **Soviet Union**, which provided the **Kosmos-3M** launch vehicle from the **Kapustin Yar** rocket launch station.
 
• The primary objective of the mission was to gain experience in building and operating a satellite system in space, which laid the groundwork for all future **Indian** space missions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Technical Specifications**: 
 
 
• The **Aryabhata** satellite weighed approximately **360 kilograms** and had a **26-sided polyhedral** structure.
 
• It was equipped with **solar panels** on all faces except the top and bottom to generate **46 watts** of power, supported by **nickel-cadmium batteries**.
 
• The mission carried three scientific experiments intended to study **X-ray astronomy**, **solar physics**, and **aeronomics**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**: 
 
 
• The satellite was named after the famous **5th-century Indian mathematician and astronomer, Aryabhata**, who pioneered concepts like the rotation of the Earth and the value of Pi.
 
• The project cost was estimated at approximately **5 crore rupees** (at the time), and the agreement for the launch was signed between **ISRO** and the **USSR Academy of Sciences** in **1972**.
 
 
 
• **Mission Duration**: 
 
 
• While the satellite was designed for a **six-month** mission life, a failure in the **electrical power system** after **five days** (and **60 orbits**) halted the scientific data transmission.
 
• Despite this, the satellite remained in orbit for **17 years** before re-entering the Earth's atmosphere on **February 11, 1992**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legacy of Aryabhata**: 
 
 
• Following the success of **Aryabhata**, India launched the **Bhaskara-I** and **Bhaskara-II** satellites in **1979** and **1981** respectively for Earth observation.
 
• The experience gained from **Aryabhata** led to the development of the **Satellite Launch Vehicle (SLV-3)**, which successfully placed the **Rohini** satellite into orbit in **1980**, making India self-reliant in launch technology.
 
 
 
• **Commemoration**: 
 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** featured the image of the **Aryabhata** satellite on the reverse side of the **two-rupee note** from **1976** to **1997** to honor this national achievement.
 
• **Satellite Technology Day**, celebrated annually on **April 19**, serves as a reminder of the dedication of **Indian** scientists who built a satellite in makeshift sheds and converted industrial estates.
 
• The **50th anniversary** in **2025** highlights India's transition from launching its first satellite on a foreign rocket to launching missions like **Chandrayaan-3** and **Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)** using indigenous technology.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In which of the following places was the regional workshop on 'Sangathan, Swasthya, Samriddhi: Women Collective’s Action on Food, Nutrition, Health and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene,' held from 22ⁿd to 23rd July 2025?

__

• The workshop was spearheaded by the **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)**, which operates under the **Ministry of Rural Development**, Government of India.
 
• The primary focus of the workshop was to integrate **Food, Nutrition, Health, and WASH** interventions into the core activities of **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** and their federations to ensure holistic rural development.
 
• It saw active participation from the **State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs)** of states including **Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal, and Chhattisgarh**, facilitating a cross-learning platform for successful community models.

• Launched in **June 2011**, this flagship program aims to reduce poverty by organizing **rural poor households** into **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** and fostering sustainable **livelihood** opportunities.
 
• The mission has a massive footprint, covering over **7,000 blocks** across India and mobilizing approximately **10 crore women** into the SHG fold.

• This is achieved through **diversification of livelihoods**, technical training, and providing **market linkages** for rural products.
 
 
 
• **FNHW Integration:**
 
 
• The **Food, Nutrition, Health, and WASH (FNHW)** vertical within DAY-NRLM leverages the social capital of women’s collectives to drive **Social and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC)**.
 
• Key activities include the promotion of **Nutri-gardens (Poshan Vatikas)**, breast-feeding practices, and **menstrual hygiene management** among rural communities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Convergence:** The mission works in convergence with the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** and the **Ministry of Jal Shakti** to achieve **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly **SDG 2 (Zero Hunger)** and **SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being)**.
 
• **Community Resource Persons (CRPs):** The workshop emphasized training **CRPs** who act as change agents at the village level, helping to monitor **nutritional outcomes** and the usage of **toilets and safe drinking water** under the **Jal Jeevan Mission**.
 
• **Regional Focus:** Conducting the workshop in **Ranchi** highlights the government's commitment to the **Eastern region**, where high rates of **malnutrition** and **anaemia** are being addressed through localized women-led strategies.

questions.question: Which of the following was the focus of the National Workshop held at Gujarat University, organised by the Ministry of Minority Affairs in July 2025?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The legendary former **Indian captain** and wicket-keeper batsman, **MS Dhoni**, was inducted into the **ICC Hall of Fame** in **June 2025**.
 
• He is celebrated for his unparalleled leadership, having led **India** to victory in three major **ICC** tournaments: the **2007 T20 World Cup**, the **2011 ODI World Cup**, and the **2013 Champions Trophy**.

• Known as "**Captain Cool**" for his composure under pressure, **Dhoni** redefined the role of a finisher in limited-overs cricket and remains the only captain in history to win all three **ICC** limited-overs trophies.
 
• His induction in **2025** follows the **ICC** guideline that typically requires a player to be retired from international cricket for at least **five years** before becoming eligible for the **Hall of Fame**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ICC Hall of Fame:**
 
 
• It was launched by the **International Cricket Council (ICC)** in **January 2009** to honor the sport's greatest players throughout history.
 
• The initiative was started in collaboration with the **Federation of International Cricketers' Associations (FICA)** as part of the **ICC's centenary celebrations**.
 
 
 
• **MS Dhoni's Career Highlights:**

• In **350 ODIs**, he scored **10,773 runs** at an average of **50.57**, and he holds the record for the most stumpings (**123**) in **ODI** history.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Bhushan** in **2018**, the **Padma Shri** in **2009**, and India's highest sporting honor, the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna**, in **2007**.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Indian Inductees:**
 
 
• Before **MS Dhoni**, other **Indian** legends inducted into the **ICC Hall of Fame** include **Bishan Singh Bedi**, **Kapil Dev**, **Sunil Gavaskar** (**2009**), **Anil Kumble** (**2015**), **Rahul Dravid** (**2018**), **Sachin Tendulkar** (**2019**), and **Virender Sehwag** (**2023**).

• **Virat Kohli:** While one of the greatest modern batsmen, **Kohli** is still active or has recently moved towards the end of his career; induction usually follows a specific **post-retirement period** of **five years**.

questions.question: Indian exports to US faced a 50% US tariff starting 27 August 2025, for buying discounted oil from ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Russia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **United States** has proposed or scheduled a **50% tariff** on Indian exports in response to India’s continued procurement of **discounted crude oil** from **Russia**.
 
• This trade measure is set to take effect starting **27 August 2025**, marking a significant escalation in trade tensions between **New Delhi** and **Washington**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Russia.***
 
• Following the **geopolitical conflict** in **Eastern Europe** that began in **2022**, **Russia** offered its oil at steep discounts to **India** to offset **Western sanctions**.
 
• **India**, the world's **third-largest** consumer of oil, increased its share of **Russian oil** imports from less than **1%** in **2021** to over **40%** by **2024**.
 
• The **US government** views the purchase of **Russian energy** as a means of providing financial support to the **Russian economy**, thereby circumventing the intended impact of **international sanctions**.
 
• The **50% tariff** specifically targets **Indian exports** to the **US market**, which is one of India's largest trading partners, to discourage further energy cooperation with **sanctioned nations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India's Energy Strategy:**
 
 
• **India** imports approximately **85%** of its total crude oil requirements to meet domestic demand.
 
• Traditionally, **Iraq**, **Saudi Arabia**, and the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)** were the top suppliers, but **Russia** surged to the **number one** spot due to competitive pricing.
 
• The **Indian government** has maintained a policy of **strategic autonomy**, prioritizing national energy security and inflation control.
 
 
 
• **Indo-US Trade Relations:**
 
 
• The **United States** is **India's** largest trading partner as of **2023-24**, with bilateral trade exceeding **$120 billion**.
 
• Key **Indian exports** to the **USA** include **pharmaceuticals**, **gems and jewelry**, **IT services**, and **textiles**.
 
• Trade disputes often arise regarding **intellectual property rights**, **market access**, and **Generalized System of Preferences (GSP)** benefits.
 
 
 
• **Global Sanctions Framework:**
 
 
• The **G7 countries** implemented a **price cap** of **$60 per barrel** on **Russian oil** to limit **Moscow's** revenue.
 
• The **US** utilizes the **Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA)** and other executive orders to influence global trade patterns.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The specific date of **27 August 2025** serves as a critical deadline for **Indian exporters** to adjust their supply chains or for **diplomatic negotiations** to resolve the tariff issue.
 
• The **50% tariff** rate is considered exceptionally high, as standard **Most Favored Nation (MFN)** rates usually range between **0% and 15%** for most industrial goods.
 
• Economists predict that such a move could lead to **trade diversion**, where **US importers** shift from **India** to other **Southeast Asian** nations like **Vietnam** or **Thailand**.
 
• **Indian refineries**, such as those operated by **Reliance Industries** and **Nayara Energy**, have been central to processing **Russian crude** into refined products for global markets.

questions.question: In June 2025, the World Bank approved a ₹3,700 crore loan for lake rejuvenation in which of the following cities of India to aid flood resilience?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengaluru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **June 2025**, the **World Bank** officially approved a massive loan amounting to **₹3,700 crore** (approximately **$440 million**) dedicated to the **rejuvenation of lakes** and the enhancement of **flood resilience** in **Bengaluru**.
 
• The project is specifically designed to address the recurring problem of **urban flooding** in the city, which is often caused by the mismanagement of **stormwater drains** and the degradation of natural water bodies. ***Hence, the correct answer is Bengaluru.***
 
• This initiative focuses on restoring the **interconnectivity** of the lake systems, which historically acted as a natural flood mitigation mechanism for the **Karnataka** state capital.
 
• The funding aims to support **nature-based solutions**, such as the creation of wetlands and the desilting of major **primary and secondary drains** (Rajakaluves) to ensure smooth water flow during heavy rainfall.
 
• The project is a collaborative effort between the **Government of Karnataka** and international financial institutions to transform the "Silicon Valley of India" into a climate-resilient megacity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The World Bank's Role in India**:
 
 
• The **World Bank** has been a long-term partner in India's urban development, providing technical expertise and **financial assistance** for infrastructure, **clean energy**, and **water management**.
 
• Headquartered in **Washington, D.C.**, the organization focuses on sustainable development goals and poverty reduction through large-scale developmental loans.
 
 
 
• **Bengaluru's Lake Ecosystem**:
 
 
• **Bengaluru**, originally known as the "City of Lakes," once possessed over **200 lakes** that were interconnected to manage the undulating terrain's water runoff.
 
• Rapid **urbanization** and **encroachment** over the last few decades have led to the disappearance of many water bodies, contributing significantly to modern-day flooding.
 
 
 
• **Flood Resilience Strategies**:
 
 
• **Flood resilience** involves building infrastructure that can withstand extreme weather events. In **India**, cities like **Chennai** and **Mumbai** have also sought similar international funding to upgrade their **drainage systems**.
 
• Strategies often include **Integrated Urban Water Management (IUWM)**, which treats the entire urban water cycle as a single system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Project Execution**: The **Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP)** and the **Karnataka Interior Department** are the primary agencies responsible for executing the rejuvenation works on the ground.
 
• **Impact on Groundwater**: Beyond flood control, the rejuvenation of these lakes is critical for **groundwater recharge**, as **Bengaluru** faces a severe **water crisis** during the summer months.
 
• **Environmental Benefits**: The restoration of lakes helps in maintaining **local biodiversity**, reducing the **urban heat island effect**, and providing recreational spaces for citizens.
 
• **Loan Terms**: The **₹3,700 crore** loan typically comes with a grace period and is part of the **International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)** lending portfolio for **India**.
